title: Chart
overview: A visual for comparison, trend, proportion, distribution, or correlation.
apply_when: The story is a relationship in a set, not a single callout number.
not_when: A table is clearer, the set is too small, or decoration.

vs.why: the data as rows; often required beside the chart

role.overview: The shape of a relationship in data — never the only channel.
role.apply_when: A trend or comparison they should see as a picture, with a table or text alternative.
role.not_when: A map of geography (map), or cell lookup (table) as the only view they need.

size.overview: Highest in the size hierarchy — the easiest to hit.
size.apply_when: The view's main instance, or full-width on a small viewport.
size.not_when: A dense toolbar or a third option next to the main control.

size.apply_when: Ordinary use in forms, pages, and chrome.
size.not_when: The only control on a mobile screen that should span the width.

size.overview: Lowest in the size hierarchy — densest.
size.apply_when: Inline or chrome that sits beside content.
size.not_when: The page's primary instance, or a control under 44×44.

composition.overview: A text or table alternative exists.

state.overview: The chart is shown with its alternative.
Geometry is not ready — skeleton or loading_indicator, not a lying axis.
state.not_when: Empty axes labeled as zero data.

accessibility.overview: A table or summary exists; the chart is not the only channel.

accessibility.not_when: Red vs green lines with no pattern or label.

keyboard.overview: Interactive legends or filters are in the tab order. A static chart is not a fake widget.
